The base URL of the npm download counts API that [`aiskills releases --downloads`](cli.md#--downloads) asks. Default: `https://api.npmjs.org`. For tests, or a mirror that serves the same paths (`/downloads/point/...`, `/downloads/range/...`, `/versions/...`). The release list itself comes from `npm view`, which uses your npm registry setting instead.

### `TERM`

Set by your terminal. When it is `dumb`, [`aiskills releases`](cli.md#releases) draws the downloads chart with `#`, as with [`--ascii`](cli.md#--ascii), and the output isn't colored.

## Colored output

On a terminal, `aiskills` colors its output; piped output is plain. See [Colored output](cli.md#colored-output). Both variables are also passed on to `npx skills`.

### `NO_COLOR`

Any non-empty value turns color off, as [`--no-color`](cli.md#--no-color) does. Wins over `FORCE_COLOR`; `--color` wins over it. The [NO_COLOR](https://no-color.org) convention.

### `FORCE_COLOR`

Any non-empty value except `0` or `false` turns color on even when the output isn't a terminal, as [`--color`](cli.md#--color) does. `NO_COLOR` and `--no-color` win over it.

## Read by `npx skills`, passed through

`aiskills` passes every variable to `npx` except npm's own `npm_*` variables (registry, proxy and certificate settings among them are kept). These are worth knowing:

| Variable | Effect in `npx skills` |
| --- | --- |
| `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK` | Turn off its anonymous usage data to `skills.sh`, and the [skills.sh install count](../concepts/install-count.md) (any value) |
| `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` | Read by `aiskills`: when set, the skills.sh install count is off |
| `npm_config_min_release_age`, `npm_config_min_release_age_exclude`, `npm_config_before` | npm's release-age rule, passed on to `npx` (other `npm_config_*` variables except registry, proxy and certificate settings are not). `npm_config_min_release_age=0 aiskills <command>` relaxes it for one run. See [When npm's release-age rule blocks the pinned version](../guides/choose-the-skills-cli-version.md#when-npms-release-age-rule-blocks-the-pinned-version) |

See also: [Set default choices](../guides/set-defaults.md) · [CLI reference](cli.md)

<!-- source: reference/files.md -->
# Files and schemas reference

What `aiskills` writes and where, and the exact fields of every file and JSON output it produces or reads; this page is exhaustive.

## The install folder

`~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/` (or [`AISKILLS_HOME`](environment.md#aiskills_home)), written by every sync (`install`, `sync`, `list` and `groups`; never by `npm install`):

```text
~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/
├── aiskills.json                     marks the folder as an aiskills folder; last sync
├── skills/                           the skills, flat or nested; replaced on every sync
├── .aiskills/layout.json             each skill's original folder
└── .claude-plugin/marketplace.json   the repo's marketplace file, used for groups
```

`skills/` is built in a temporary `.skills.tmp-<pid>` folder next to it, then swapped in.

## `aiskills.json`

```json
{
  "package": "@sugatoray-ai/aiskills",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "layout": "flat",
  "installedAt": "2026-11-06T10:26:01.152Z",
  "skills": "/home/me/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills"
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | Always `@sugatoray-ai/aiskills`. Its presence is what makes a folder safe for `aiskills` to replace or delete. |
| `version` | string | The package version that wrote the folder. |
| `layout` | `"flat"` \| `"nested"` | The layout of `skills/`, reused by the next sync unless overridden. |
| `stats` | boolean, optional | Written by `--stats` / `--no-stats`: whether `aiskills install` adds installs to the [skills.sh count](../concepts/install-count.md). Kept by later syncs; absent means on. |
| `installedAt` | string (ISO 8601) | When the folder was last synced. |
| `skills` | string (absolute path) | The `skills/` folder. |

## Config files

Written by [`aiskills config`](cli.md#config). Each is a JSON object of key → value, for example `{"agents": "claude-code,codex", "layout": "nested"}`; the keys and values are listed under [`config`](cli.md#config).

| File | Written by | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills.json` | `aiskills config <key> <value>` (`--global`) | Your defaults. Outside the install folder, so `uninstall --purge` keeps it, and `AISKILLS_HOME` doesn't move it. |
| `./.aiskills.json` | `aiskills config --project <key> <value>` | Defaults for the current folder; win over the user file. Commit it to share them with a project. |

Keys `aiskills` doesn't know (from a newer version) are ignored. A file that isn't valid JSON stops every command that reads settings, with [`is not valid JSON`](errors.md#config-file-not-valid-json).

## `.aiskills/layout.json`

Written when the package is built, and copied to the install folder.

```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "description": "skills/ is flat (skills/<name>/). …",
  "skills": {
    "create-lib-docs": "docs/create-lib-docs",
    "scrolls-setup": "scrolls/scrolls-setup"
  },
  "extras": ["scrolls/README.md", "scrolls/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"],
  "ignored": ["newsletters/newsletter-ai/"]
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | number | Version of this file's shape; currently `1`. |
| `description` | string | A note for people reading the file. |
| `skills` | object: skill name → string | Each skill's original folder, relative to the repo's `skills/`. Used for `--nested` and for groups. |
| `extras` | string[] | Files outside any skill folder (READMEs, `plugin.json`, `meta/`), stored in the package under `.aiskills/nested/` at these paths. |
| `ignored` | string[] | Paths a `.skillsignore` left out of the package. Folders end with `/`. In this version: `newsletters/newsletter-ai/`, from `skills/newsletters/.skillsignore`. |

## The package

```text
@sugatoray-ai/aiskills/
├── bin/aiskills.mjs, bin/aix.mjs     the commands (aiskills and ais share one file)
├── src/scripts/core/                 cli.mjs, installer.mjs
├── skills/<skill>/                   the skills, flat
├── .aiskills/layout.json, .aiskills/nested/
├── .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
└── README.md, CHANGELOG.md, SECURITY.md, LICENSE, package.json
```

That is everything the package contains. What builds it stays in the repo: `src/scripts/pack/` (copies the skills in at `npm pack`), `src/scripts/docs/` (builds these docs and the banner), `src/test/` and `docs/`.

Files named `.gitignore` and `.npmignore` inside the skills are stored as `_gitignore` and `_npmignore`, because npm drops the real names; every sync renames them back. The package has no JavaScript API: only the commands are public.

## `aiskills groups --json`

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "name": "scrolls-skills",
      "alias": "scrolls",
      "description": "Scrolls: a git-native markdown system …",
      "skills": ["scrolls-help", "scrolls-hide", "…"]
    }
  ],
  "ungrouped": []
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `groups[].name` | string | The group name from `marketplace.json`. |
| `groups[].alias` | string | The name without a trailing `-skills`. |
| `groups[].description` | string | From `marketplace.json`; may be empty. |
| `groups[].skills` | string[] | Skill names, sorted. |
| `ungrouped` | string[] | Bundled skills in no group, sorted. |

## `npx skills list --json` rows

`aiskills` reads these (from `npx skills list --json [--global]`) to know what is installed. It never writes them. Fields as reported by `skills@1.7.6`:

| Field | Type | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | The skill name. |
| `source` | string | Where it was installed from: a folder path, or `owner/repo`. |
| `sourceType` | string | `local` for a folder, `github` for GitHub. |
| `scope` | string | `global` or `project`. |
| `agents` | string[] | Agents it's installed for, as display names such as `Claude Code` (shown by `installed`). |
| `path`, `sourceUrl`, `status` | string | Also present in `skills@1.7.6`; not used by `aiskills`. |

A row is **from this package** when `sourceType` is `local` and `source` is the install folder.

## Written by `npx skills`

The agents' skill folders (`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, …, or the project's with `-p`) and `npx skills`' own records, such as a project's `skills-lock.json`. `aiskills` doesn't touch them directly.

See also: [How aiskills works](../concepts/how-it-works.md) · [Layouts](../concepts/layouts.md)

<!-- source: reference/skillsignore.md -->
# `.skillsignore` reference

The rule syntax of `.skillsignore` files, which leave files, folders or whole skills out of the package when it is built; this page is exhaustive.

A `.skillsignore` can sit in the repo's `skills/` folder or any folder below it. Its rules apply to that folder and below. It is read only when the package is built (`npm pack`), so it matters to maintainers, not to users. The repo uses one: `skills/newsletters/.skillsignore` holds `newsletter-ai/`, which leaves that skill out of the package (it stays installable from the repo with `npx skills add`).

## Syntax

The syntax is a subset of `.gitignore`:

| Line | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| blank, or starting with `#` | Skipped. A `#` later in a line is part of the pattern. |
| `\#name`, `\!name` | A literal leading `#` or `!`. |
| `name` | A file or folder with that name, at any depth. |
| `/name`, `a/name` | A leading or middle `/` anchors the pattern to the `.skillsignore`'s folder. |
| `name/` | Folders only. |
| `*`, `?`, `[abc]`, `[!abc]` | Within one path segment. |
| `**` | Across segments: `**/x`, `x/**`, `a/**/b`. |
| `!pattern` | Re-include something an earlier rule excluded. |

## Rules

- **The last matching rule wins.** Rules in a deeper `.skillsignore` come after the outer ones.
- **An ignored folder is never entered**, so a file inside it can't be re-included (as in git).
- **`.skillsignore` files never ship.**
- **Ignoring only a `SKILL.md` is refused.** Ignore the skill's folder to drop the skill.
- **What was left out** is listed under `ignored` in [`.aiskills/layout.json`](files.md#aiskillslayoutjson).

## Example

```gitignore
# every tests/ folder, at any depth
**/tests/
# a "/" in the middle anchors to this folder, so use **/ for any depth
**/meta/MAINTAINERS.md
# all .log files except keep.log
*.log
!keep.log
# ignoring a skill's folder drops the whole skill
scrolls/wip-skill/
```

See also: [Leave files out of the package](../guides/leave-files-out.md) · [Errors](errors.md#packaging-errors-maintainers)

<!-- source: reference/errors.md -->
# Errors and exit codes reference

Every error and warning `aiskills` prints, with its cause and fix, and what each exit code means; this page is exhaustive.

Errors and warnings go to stderr and start with `[aiskills]`. Parts in `<angle brackets>` vary.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Success. `uninstall` also exits `0` when there was nothing to remove. |
| `1` | `aiskills` stopped with one of the errors below, or `installed` couldn't read `npx skills list`. No skill was installed or removed. |
| any other | The exit code of the `npx skills` command it ran, passed through. |

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install --purge
```

```text
[aiskills] option --purge is not valid here
```

## Options and commands

### Option not valid here

```text
[aiskills] option <option> is not valid here
```

**Cause:** the option exists, but not for this command, e.g. `--purge` on `install`. **Fix:** see which options each command takes in the [CLI reference](cli.md#options).

### Unknown option

```text
[aiskills] unknown option: <option>
```

**Cause:** a typo, or an option of `npx skills` given directly. **Fix:** check `aiskills --help`; pass `npx skills` options after `--`.

### Option needs a value

```text
[aiskills] <option> needs a value
```

**Cause:** `-a`, `-s` or `-G` is the last argument. **Fix:** add the value: `-s scrolls-setup`.

### Unknown command

```text
unknown command: <name>
```

**Cause:** not one of the [commands](cli.md#commands). The help follows on stderr. **Fix:** check the spelling; `aiskills help` lists them.

## Choosing skills, groups and agents

### Not provided by this package

```text
[aiskills] not provided by this package: <names>
  available: <bundled skills>
  add --route to look them up with 'npx skills' instead
```

**Cause:** `install -s` names a skill that isn't bundled. **Fix:** check the spelling against `available`, or add `--route` (or use `aix`) for an external skill. On `uninstall` the last line reads `use --route to also match skills installed from other sources, or -f/--force`.

### No skill matches

```text
[aiskills] no skill matches: <patterns>
  available: <skills>
```

**Cause:** an `-s` pattern matched no skill. **Fix:** adjust the pattern; patterns match the whole name, ignoring case.

### No group matches

```text
[aiskills] no group matches: <names>
  available: <group (alias), …>, all
  see 'aiskills groups'
```

**Cause:** a `-G` name, alias or pattern matched no group. **Fix:** pick one from `available`.

### The selected groups contain no skills

```text
[aiskills] the selected group(s) contain no skills
```

**Cause:** the `-G` groups exist but have no bundled skills. **Fix:** choose other groups; `aiskills groups` shows each group's skills.

### No marketplace.json

```text
[aiskills] no .claude-plugin/marketplace.json in <install folder>; run 'aiskills sync' first
```

**Cause:** `-G` was used but the install folder has no `marketplace.json`, e.g. it was synced by an older version. **Fix:** `aiskills sync`.

### No agent matches

```text
[aiskills] no agent matches: <patterns>
  valid agents: <agents>
```

**Cause:** an `-a` pattern matched none of the agents `npx skills` supports. **Fix:** adjust the pattern, or use names from `valid agents`.

### No agents recorded (`--last-agents`)

```text
[aiskills] --last-agents: no agents recorded in <lock file>
  pick them once with 'aiskills install -i' (or 'npx skills add'), or use -a <agents>
```

**Cause:** `--last-agents` reads `lastSelectedAgents` from the lock file `npx skills` keeps (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/skills/.skill-lock.json`, else `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`), and it has none: the agent picker of `npx skills add` was never used. **Fix:** run `aiskills install -i` once and pick the agents, or name them with `-a`.

### Interactive install needs a terminal

```text
[aiskills] -i/--interactive needs a terminal; pick with -s/-G/-a instead
```

**Cause:** `-i` lets `npx skills add` ask which skills and agents to use, and there is no terminal to ask in (a script, CI, an agent). Nothing is installed. **Fix:** drop `-i` and choose with `-s`, `-G`, `-a` or `-l`/`--last-agents`.

### Could not read the agent list

```text
[aiskills] could not read the agent list from 'npx skills'
```

**Cause:** an `-a` pattern needs the agent list, and `npx skills` didn't print it (no network for the first download, or a `skills` version that words it differently). **Fix:** pass plain agent names instead of a pattern, or go back to the pinned `skills` version.

## Uninstall

### Purge only with a full uninstall

```text
[aiskills] --purge only applies to a full uninstall (drop -s/-G)
```

**Cause:** `--purge` with `-s` or `-G`. **Fix:** remove the skills first, then run `aiskills uninstall --purge` on its own.

### Names a source, not a skill

```text
[aiskills] '<entry>' names a source, not a skill; use -s <skill> or <owner/repo@skill>
```

**Cause:** `--route uninstall -s owner/repo`: a repository isn't a skill name. **Fix:** name the skill, `-s pdf` or `-s owner/repo@pdf`.

### Not installed, skipping

```text
[aiskills] not installed (<scope>), skipping: <names>
```

**Warning.** **Cause:** with `--route`, these names aren't installed in this scope. **Fix:** none needed; check `-g`/`-p` if you expected them.

### Could not read `npx skills list` (uninstall)

```text
[aiskills] could not read 'npx skills list'; falling back to the skills found in <install folder>
```

**Warning.** **Cause:** `npx skills list --json` failed during a full uninstall, so `aiskills` removes every skill name in its folder instead. **Fix:** usually none; check network access if it repeats.

### Could not read `npx skills list` (installed)

```text
[aiskills] could not read 'npx skills list'
```

**Cause:** `installed` couldn't run or parse `npx skills list --json`; exit code `1`. **Fix:** run `aiskills skills list -g` to see the underlying error.

## External skills (`--route`)

### Matches several skills

```text
[aiskills] '<name>' matches several skills; pick one with -s <owner/repo@skill>:
    <owner/repo@name>  (<installs>)
    …
```

**Cause:** more than one registry result has exactly this name. `aiskills` never picks. **Fix:** choose one and pass it as `-s owner/repo@name`.

### No skill named exactly

```text
[aiskills] no skill named exactly '<name>'; closest results:
    <owner/repo@skill>  (<installs>)
```

**Cause:** the registry has similar skills but none with this exact name. **Fix:** use one of the listed names, or `aiskills find <query>` to search.

### No skill found

```text
[aiskills] no skill named '<name>' found by 'npx skills find'
```

**Cause:** the registry returned nothing (or there's no network access to `skills.sh`). **Fix:** check the name and network, or give the source as `owner/repo@skill`.

### Unsafe registry results ignored

```text
[aiskills] ignored <n> registry result(s) with unsafe characters: "<spec>", …
```

**Warning.** **Cause:** results whose `owner/repo@skill` has characters other than letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` are never used. **Fix:** none needed. If the skill you want was among them, check its source and pass it yourself.

### Not confirmed (no terminal)

```text
[aiskills] found in the skills registry (not bundled; third-party code your agents may run):
    <owner/repo@skill>  (<n> installs)  for '<name>'
[aiskills] not installing external skills without confirmation: <owner/repo@skill>, …
  re-run with -y/--yes to install them, or pin each one with -s owner/repo@skill
```

**Cause:** `--route` (or `aix`) found a skill by looking up a bare name, and there is no terminal to ask in (a script, CI, an agent). Nothing was installed, not even bundled skills. **Fix:** check the listed source, then re-run with [`-y`](cli.md#-y---yes), or pin it: `-s <owner/repo@skill>`.

### Not confirmed

```text
Install <n> external skill(s) from the registry? [y/N] n
[aiskills] nothing installed: not confirmed
```

**Cause:** you answered anything but `y` or `yes` (Enter means no). Nothing was installed. **Fix:** none needed. To install, run again and answer `y`, or pin the skill as `owner/repo@skill`.

## Files and folders

### Not an aiskills folder

```text
[aiskills] <folder> is not an aiskills folder (it has other files but no aiskills.json), so it won't be replaced or deleted.
  Point AISKILLS_HOME at a new or empty folder instead.
```

**Cause:** the install folder (usually from `AISKILLS_HOME`) already holds files that `aiskills` didn't write. **Fix:** point `AISKILLS_HOME` at a new or empty folder, or unset it.

### Unknown layout

```text
[aiskills] unknown layout '<value>' (use flat or nested)
```

**Cause:** `AISKILLS_LAYOUT`, or the `layout` in `aiskills.json`, isn't `flat` or `nested`. **Fix:** set `AISKILLS_LAYOUT=flat` or `nested`, or run `aiskills sync --flat`.

### AISKILLS_STATS must be 1 or 0

```text
[aiskills] AISKILLS_STATS must be 1 or 0 (or true/false, yes/no, on/off); got '<value>'
```

**Cause:** `AISKILLS_STATS` is set to something else. **Fix:** set it to `0` (or `1`), or unset it. See [The skills.sh install count](../concepts/install-count.md).

### No vendored skills folder

```text
[aiskills] no vendored skills folder at <package>/skills
```

**Cause:** the package has no `skills/`, which happens when running from a git checkout of the repo. **Fix:** install the published package, or run `npm run vendor` in the checkout.

### Nested layout unavailable

```text
[aiskills] this package has no .aiskills/layout.json, so --nested can't rebuild the nested layout
```

**Cause:** the package was built without `layout.json`. **Fix:** use `--flat`, or reinstall the published package.

## Releases and downloads

### Invalid number of releases

```text
[aiskills] invalid number of releases '<value>' (use a whole number of 1 or more, or all)
```

**Cause:** the number after `aiskills releases` or `-L`/`--last` isn't a whole number of 1 or more, or `all`. **Fix:** `aiskills rel 10`, `aiskills rel all`.

### Invalid period

```text
[aiskills] invalid period '<value>'
  use all, <N><d|w|m|y> (7d, 2w, 1m = 30 days, 1y = 365 days), <YYYY-MM-DD>:<YYYY-MM-DD> or <YYYY-MM-DD>:
```

**Cause:** the value of `--downloads` isn't one of the [period forms](cli.md#--downloads): for example `7days`, `1.5m`, `0d`, an impossible date, or a range whose start is after its end. Checked before any network call. **Fix:** use one of the listed forms.

### No download counts after a date

```text
[aiskills] npm has no download counts after <date>; pick a period that starts on or before it
```

**Cause:** a `--downloads` range starts after npm's latest day of data (usually yesterday). **Fix:** start the range earlier, or use `<N>d`.

### `--chart` and `--table` together

```text
[aiskills] --chart and --table can't be used together
```

**Cause:** both were given. **Fix:** pick one; `--chart` is the default.

### Bad `--by` value

```text
[aiskills] --by takes day, week or month; got '<value>'
```

**Cause:** `--by` was given something else, or nothing. **Fix:** `--by day`, `--by week` or `--by month`.

### Could not read the releases

```text
[aiskills] could not read the releases of @sugatoray-ai/aiskills from <registry>: <npm's reason>
```

**Cause:** `npm view` failed: no network, a registry (or company mirror) that doesn't have the package or refuses the request, or npm missing from `PATH` (then `<registry>` reads `npm`). `<registry>` is what `npm config get registry` reports, so you can see which one was asked. If npm answered with something other than JSON, the reason is `unexpected output from 'npm view'` (`... from npm: unexpected output from 'npm view'`). On `info --full` the same message appears as `latest on npm : unavailable` and `info` still succeeds. **Fix:** check `npm view @sugatoray-ai/aiskills version` works, and your registry setting (`npm config get registry`). Behind a mirror, ask whoever runs it to proxy the public npm registry for `@sugatoray-ai/aiskills`.

### Could not reach api.npmjs.org

```text
[aiskills] could not reach api.npmjs.org: <reason>
```

**Cause:** `--downloads` couldn't get an answer from the download counts API: no network, a firewall or proxy that blocks the host, an HTTP error (`HTTP 503`), or an answer it can't use (`could not reach api.npmjs.org: the answer was not JSON`, `could not reach api.npmjs.org: no latest day in its answer`). A proxy in `HTTPS_PROXY` is used on Node versions that support `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` (22.21+, 24+). Registry mirrors (Artifactory, Nexus, Verdaccio) don't serve download counts, so a network that only allows a mirror can't use `--downloads`. Behind a TLS-inspecting proxy, `npm` uses its `cafile`/`ca` settings but these requests run in Node, which reads extra certificates from `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` (a PEM file); without it the reason is a certificate error such as `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN` or `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY`. **Fix:** run without `--downloads`; allow `api.npmjs.org`; set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to your company's CA bundle; or, if your company proxies api.npmjs.org, point [`AISKILLS_NPM_API_URL`](environment.md#aiskills_npm_api_url) at it.

### Bad `AISKILLS_TODAY`

```text
[aiskills] AISKILLS_TODAY must be a date (YYYY-MM-DD); got '<value>'
```

**Cause:** [`AISKILLS_TODAY`](environment.md#aiskills_today) is set to something that isn't a real date. **Fix:** a date like `2026-11-12`, or unset it.

## Config errors

From [`aiskills config`](cli.md#config), and from any command that reads a config file.

### Unknown config key

```text
unknown config key: <key> (keys: agents, color, copy, groups, layout, route, scope, skills, skills-version, stats)
```

**Fix:** use one of the listed keys. Keys are lowercase and use a hyphen (`skills-version`).

### Value not valid for the key

```text
<key> must be <values>; got '<value>'
<key> must be true or false (or yes/no, on/off, 1/0); got '<value>'
<key> needs at least one name
<key> needs a value
skills-version must be a version (e.g. 1.7.6), "latest", "next", an npm range (e.g. ~1.7.4) or an interval (e.g. [1.7.4, 1.8.0)); got '<value>'
```

**Fix:** give a value the key takes; the [keys table](cli.md#config) lists them. Nothing is written.

### Not set

```text
<key> is not set in <file>
```

**Fix:** `--unset` only removes what that file holds. Check with `aiskills config --list --show-origin`, and add `--project` for `./.aiskills.json`.

### Config file not valid JSON

```text
<file> is not valid JSON; fix it or delete it
<file>: <key> must be ...
```

**Fix:** a config file is a JSON object such as `{"layout": "nested"}`. Correct the file, or delete it and set the values again. Any command that reads settings stops on it, so the broken file doesn't silently stop counting.

### Config usage

```text
usage: aiskills config <key> [<value>] | --unset <key> | --list [--show-origin] [--json]  [--global | --project]
```

**Fix:** pass a key (to read), a key and a value (to set), `--unset <key>`, or `--list`.

## Upgrade

### Can't upgrade

```text
[aiskills] can't upgrade: <how aiskills was run, and what to do>
```

**Cause:** this aiskills isn't a global install, so there's nothing for `upgrade` to replace. It was run through npx (`npx @sugatoray-ai/aiskills@latest install` gets the latest), is a project's dependency (`npm install -D @sugatoray-ai/aiskills@latest`; your lockfile pins it), or is a source checkout (`git pull`, or `npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills`). The message names which. **Fix:** the command it gives. `aiskills upgrade --check` still works.

### No such version or tag

```text
[aiskills] no version or tag '<value>' of @sugatoray-ai/aiskills on the registry (see: aiskills releases all)
```

**Cause:** the `<version>` or `<tag>` given to `upgrade` isn't on the registry npm uses. If the registry reports no `latest` tag at all, the message is `the registry reports no latest version of @sugatoray-ai/aiskills`. **Fix:** pick one from `aiskills releases all`.

### Downgrade not confirmed

```text
[aiskills] not downgrading <installed> → <target> without confirmation: re-run with -y
```

**Cause:** the target is older than the installed version (`--check` says `installed <version> is newer than <target>`), and there was no terminal to ask in (or the answer to `[y/N]` wasn't yes: `nothing changed: not confirmed`). **Fix:** add `-y` if you mean it.

### Bad `upgrade` options

```text
[aiskills] --json only works with --check
[aiskills] give one version or tag (got '<a>' and '<b>')
```

**Cause:** `--json` without `--check`, or two targets. **Fix:** `aiskills upgrade --check --json`; one target.

### The package manager failed

```text
npm has no permission to write its global folder. Don't use sudo; give npm a folder you own:
  npm config set prefix ~/.npm-global   (then add ~/.npm-global/bin to PATH and install aiskills again)
```

**Cause:** the global install failed; `upgrade` exits with its exit code and nothing else changes. A permission error (`EACCES`) gets the hint above; npm's release-age rule gets [its usual explanation](#npms-release-age-rule-blocked-the-skills-cli); if the package manager can't be started at all: `could not run <npm|pnpm|bun|yarn>: <reason>`. **Fix:** as shown; then run `aiskills upgrade` again.

### Refresh warnings

```text
[aiskills] could not read 'npx skills list'; the skills won't be refreshed
[aiskills] couldn't tell which agent '<name>' is; re-add its skills with: aiskills install -s <skills> -a <agent id>
[aiskills] <npm> installed <version>, not <target>
```

**Cause:** after the upgrade, aiskills couldn't list what's installed (no network for `npx`), couldn't map an agent's display name to an id, or the package manager installed a different version than asked (a registry or mirror lagging behind). The upgrade itself succeeded. **Fix:** run the `aiskills install` command for the skills and agents shown (to see the agent ids, give `-a` a pattern that matches none: `aiskills install -a 'x*' -n` stops with `no agent matches` and lists every valid id).

## Running `npx skills`

### Bad `AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION`

```text
[aiskills] AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION must be a version (e.g. 1.7.6), "latest", "next", an npm range (e.g. ~1.7.4) or an interval (e.g. [1.7.4, 1.8.0)); got '<value>'
```

**Cause:** tags other than `latest`/`next`, URLs, paths, shell syntax, tabs, line breaks or Unicode spaces between a range's parts, and malformed intervals (an open end `…` needs `(` or `)`) are refused. **Fix:** use one of the forms in [Choose the `skills` CLI version](../guides/choose-the-skills-cli-version.md#variations), or unset it for the pinned one.

### `skills` CLI version overridden

```text
[aiskills] using skills@<spec> from AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION, not the tested 1.7.6
```

**Cause:** a notice, not an error: `AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION` is set to something other than the pinned version, so `npx` runs a `skills` CLI nobody tested with `aiskills`. **Fix:** if you didn't set it, look for it in your shell profile, a project's `.envrc`/`.env`, or CI variables, and unset it.

### Empty `AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION` interval

```text
[aiskills] AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION '<value>' is an empty interval: no version fits it
```

**Cause:** the lower bound is above the upper one, or they're equal and not both inclusive (`[1.7.6, 1.7.6)`). **Fix:** swap or widen the bounds; `[1.7.6, 1.7.6]` means exactly `1.7.6`.

### npm's release-age rule blocked the `skills` CLI

```text
npm error notarget No matching version found for skills@1.7.6 with a date before 11/2/2026, 9:53:24 AM.
[aiskills] npm's release-age rule (min-release-age or before) blocked skills@1.7.6: npm only installs versions published before 11/2/2026, 9:53:24 AM, and this one is newer.
[aiskills]   - wait until it is old enough ('npm view skills time' shows when each version came out), or
[aiskills]   - relax the rule for one run: npm_config_min_release_age=0 aiskills <command>, or
[aiskills]   - allow an older, untested skills CLI: AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION='(..., 1.7.6]' (npm picks the newest it may)
```

**Cause:** your `.npmrc` (or environment) sets `min-release-age` or `before`, and the `skills` CLI version `aiskills` runs was published more recently. npm's `min-release-age-exclude` doesn't apply to `npx`. With a range in `AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION`, the last line instead suggests a wider range. **Fix:** one of the three lines; see [When npm's release-age rule blocks the pinned version](../guides/choose-the-skills-cli-version.md#when-npms-release-age-rule-blocks-the-pinned-version).

### Shell characters on Windows

```text
[aiskills] refusing to pass shell characters to cmd.exe: <arguments>
```

**Cause:** on Windows, an argument contains one of `& | < > ^ % ! " ( )`, which `cmd.exe` would interpret. The `skills@<range>` argument from `AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION` is the one exception: it's already limited to version characters and is passed in double quotes. **Fix:** remove those characters; skill names and specs never need them.

## Packaging errors (maintainers)

These come from `npm pack` / `npm run vendor`, when the package is built from the repo.

### Repo not found

```text
no ancestor of <folder> contains skills/ and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
```

**Fix:** build from inside the repo, where `skills/` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` are above the package folder.

### `skills/` not found

```text
<repo>/skills not found
```

**Fix:** the repo's `skills/` folder is missing; restore it.

### SKILL.md ignored

```text
.skillsignore ignores <group>/<skill>/SKILL.md; to drop a skill, ignore the folder (<group>/<skill>/) instead
```

**Fix:** ignore the skill's folder, not only its `SKILL.md`. See [`.skillsignore`](skillsignore.md).

### Skill directly in `skills/`

```text
<repo>/skills/SKILL.md: a skill can't sit directly in skills/
```

**Fix:** move the skill into its own folder.

### Skill inside a skill

```text
skills inside other skills aren't supported: <folders>
```

**Fix:** move the inner skill out to its own folder.

### Unsafe skill name

```text
skills/<folder>: skill name '<name>' can't be used as a folder name
```

**Fix:** use only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` in the `name:`.

### Duplicate skill name

```text
two skills are both named '<name>': skills/<folder> and skills/<folder>
```

**Fix:** give one of them another `name:`.

## Docs build errors (maintainers)

These come from `npm run docs:html`, which builds `docs/docsite/index.html`.

### Page not in the landing page

```text
pages not linked from a section of README.md: <pages>
```

**Fix:** add each page to a `### Section` list in `docs/docsite/README.md` (`- [Title](path.md): summary`). The tabs are built from those lists.

### Usage

```text
usage: build-docs-html.mjs <docs-dir> --out <file.html> [--ref <branch>] [--version <v>] [--menu <json>]
```

**Fix:** pass the docs folder and `--out`, or use `npm run docs:html`.

### Version menu

```text
version menu: --menu is not valid JSON
version menu: unknown kind: <kind> (dev, latest or older)
version menu: needs exactly one latest release
version menu: <version> is not one of its versions
```

**Fix:** `--menu` is JSON: `{"current": "<this page's version>", "base": "<path to the site root>", "entries": [{"version", "path", "kind"}]}`, with one `latest` entry, and the current version among the entries. `npm run docs:site` writes it for you.

### CLI outputs page

```text
usage: create-cli-outputs.mjs [--check] [--out <file>]
<file> is out of date: run npm run cli-outputs
create-cli-outputs needs a POSIX shell for the stand-in npx and npm
```

**Fix:** run `npm run cli-outputs` (or `npm run docs`) after a change that alters what a command prints, and commit `docs/docsite/reference/cli-outputs.html`. The page is built by running every command in `docs/cli-outputs/commands.json` with stand-in `npx` and `npm` scripts, so build it on macOS, Linux or WSL.

### Site build usage

```text
usage: build-site.mjs --out <dir> [--ref <branch>] [--releases <n>|all]
unknown argument: <argument>
--releases must be a whole number of at least 1, or all: <value>
```

**Fix:** pass the output folder, or use `npm run docs:site`, which writes `site/`. `--releases` is how many releases the site shows, the latest included (default 5). It reads the release tags (`aiskills-vX.Y.Z`) with git, so run it in a clone that has them (`git fetch --tags`).

## Banner build errors (maintainers)

These come from `npm run banner`, `banner:check` and `banner:png` (`src/scripts/docs/create-banner.mjs`), and from `npm run docs:html`, which copies the banner onto the docs landing page.

### Config value not quoted

```text
config line <n>: values must be double-quoted strings: <text>
```

**Fix:** in `docs/banner/config.yaml`, write every value as `key: "value"`, and list items as `  - "item"`.

### Config line not understood

```text
config line <n>: expected 'key: "value"' or a '  - "item"' line
config line <n>: a list item without a key above it
```

**Fix:** use only `key: "value"`, `key:` followed by `  - "item"` lines, blank lines and `#` comments.

### Unknown `--set` key

```text
--set: unknown key: <key>
```

**Fix:** use a key that exists in `config.yaml`.

### Install style or count

```text
install_style must be "box" or "chips", not "<value>"
install_style "<style>" has room for 1 to <max> install commands, not <n>
```

**Fix:** `box` takes up to 3 commands and `chips` up to 2.

### Unknown theme

```text
unknown theme: <name> (use one of teal, paper, phosphor, …, lightsout)
```

**Fix:** set `theme` in `docs/banner/config.yaml` (or `--set theme=…`) to one of the themes in `src/scripts/docs/themes.mjs`. The default is `lightsout`.

### Demo group or skill

```text
demo_group "<name>" isn't a bundled group (<aliases>)
route_skill "<name>" is bundled, so 'aix i -s <name>' wouldn't look it up
```

**Fix:** `demo_group` must be a bundled group; `route_skill` must be a skill the package does *not* bundle, or the terminal demo would show something `aiskills` doesn't do.

### Template placeholder without a value

```text
template placeholder {{ <name> }} has no value
```

**Fix:** a placeholder was added to `src/scripts/docs/templates/banner-template.html` without a value in `render()`; add one.

### PNG needs Playwright

```text
--png needs Playwright (npm install -g playwright, then npx playwright install chromium)
--scale must be 1, 2 or 4
```

**Fix:** install Playwright and Chromium, and use scale 1, 2 or 4.

### Page out of date

```text
<path>/aiskills-banner.html is out of date: run npm run banner
```

**Fix:** run `npm run banner` (and `npm run banner:png` for the README image), then `npm run docs:html`.

### Banner page missing (docs build)

```text
banner page not found: <path> (run npm run banner, or pass --no-banner)
<path>: no banner:html:start ... banner:html:end markers
```

**Fix:** build the banner page first, or build the docs with `--no-banner`. Keep the `banner:html` and `banner:css` marker comments in the template.

See also: [Use aiskills from an AI agent or a script](../guides/use-from-an-agent.md) · [FAQ and troubleshooting](../faq.md)

<!-- source: faq.md -->
# FAQ and troubleshooting

Answers to the questions people ask most, and fixes for the problems they hit.

## Questions

### Which agents are supported?

Every agent the `skills` CLI supports: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Qoder and many more. `aiskills` reads the list from `npx skills`, so a newer `skills` version brings new agents with no change here. Pass agent ids to `-a` (`claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, …).

### Does `aiskills install` put the skills in every agent's folder?

No, only in the agents `npx skills` detects: those whose folder already exists (such as `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`), plus the agents that share `~/.config/agents/skills`. Only when it detects none does it install for every agent it supports, creating a folder for each. To choose yourself, name agents with `-a`, pick them from a list with [`-i`](reference/cli.md#-i---interactive), or reuse your last pick with [`-l`](reference/cli.md#-l---last-agents). See [2. Pick skills and agents](tutorial/02-pick-skills-and-agents.md#pick-from-a-list--i).

### Where are the skills on my machine?

The saved copy is in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/` (`aiskills path` prints the folder). `npx skills` installs them into each agent's own folder, such as `~/.claude/skills/`, or the project's folders with `-p`.

### What's the difference between `aiskills`, `ais` and `aix`?

`ais` is `aiskills`. `aix` is `aiskills --route`, which also manages skills that aren't bundled. See [Bundled and external skills](concepts/bundled-and-external.md).

### How do I update the skills?

Run `aiskills upgrade`. It installs the latest aiskills with the package manager you installed it with, then updates the skills your agents have, for the same agents. Skills that are new in that version are listed with the commands to add them. `aiskills upgrade --check` only says whether there is a newer version. (Before 0.9.0: `npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills@latest`, then `aiskills install` again.) See [`upgrade`](reference/cli.md#upgrade).

### How do I see my setup, or check for a newer version?

`aiskills info` shows the aiskills version, the install folder, what was saved there and by which version, and every setting with where its value comes from (a flag's default, an `AISKILLS_*` variable, or remembered). It is offline; `aiskills info --full` also asks npm for the latest version. `aiskills rel` lists the latest releases on npm and marks the one you have; `aiskills rel --downloads` adds download counts. See [`info`](reference/cli.md#info) and [`releases`](reference/cli.md#releases).

### Does aiskills work behind a firewall or with an npm mirror?

Yes, except for download counts. Everything goes through npm and your npm config (`registry=`, proxy, `cafile`), so a company mirror (Artifactory, Nexus, Verdaccio, …) works:

| Command | Needs | With only an npm mirror |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install`, `uninstall`, `installed`, `list`, `skills` | the `skills` package, through `npx` | works |
| `info` | nothing (local files) | works |
| `info --full` | `npm view`, and `skills` through `npx` | works |
| `releases` / `rel` | `npm view` | works; a mirror that strips publish times shows `–` as the date and says so |
| `rel --downloads` | api.npmjs.org | fails with `could not reach api.npmjs.org`; mirrors don't serve download counts ([fixes](reference/errors.md#could-not-reach-apinpmjsorg)) |
| the skills.sh install count | github.com | skipped silently; the install is unaffected |
| `--route` / `aix` lookups | skills.sh | fail with an error; bundled skills don't need them |

The `changelog:` line of `aiskills rel` is only printed, never fetched; its first path is the copy inside the installed package, readable offline. A TLS-inspecting proxy needs `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for `--downloads` (npm itself uses `cafile`).

### Why are download counts per version only for the last 7 days?

Because npm only keeps per-version counts for the last 7 days; older ones aren't stored anywhere. `aiskills rel --downloads <period>` shows them in a column, and the package's total (all versions together) for any period, from all time (`all`, the default) to a day (`1d`). See [`--downloads`](reference/cli.md#--downloads).

### Does it install Claude Code plugins?

No. It reads the repo's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` only to group the skills. Everything is installed as skills through `npx skills`.

### Can I edit the saved skills?

Don't: every sync replaces `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/`. Copy a skill elsewhere to change it, or contribute the change to [the repo](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills).

### Does aiskills send any data?

`aiskills` sends nothing itself. After `aiskills install`, it runs `npx skills add sugatoray/aiskills` once more in a temp folder, in the background, so the install is counted on skills.sh (off with `--no-stats` or `AISKILLS_STATS=0`); see [The skills.sh install count](concepts/install-count.md). The `skills` CLI sends anonymous usage data to `skills.sh` unless `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` or `DO_NOT_TRACK` is set, and either one also turns the count off. See [Security model](concepts/security.md#telemetry).

### `aiskills` fails with "No matching version found for skills@… with a date before …"

Your npm has a release-age rule (`min-release-age` or `before` in `.npmrc`), and the `skills` CLI version `aiskills` runs is newer than it allows. `aiskills` prints the options after npm's error: wait, run once with `npm_config_min_release_age=0 aiskills <command>`, or set `AISKILLS_SKILLS_LIB_VERSION='(..., 1.7.6]'` so npm can fall back to an older version. See [When npm's release-age rule blocks the pinned version](guides/choose-the-skills-cli-version.md#when-npms-release-age-rule-blocks-the-pinned-version).

### Why don't my installs show up on skills.sh?

The count needs github.com and api.github.com: without them it's skipped silently. It's also off with `--no-stats` (check `"stats"` in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/aiskills.json`), `AISKILLS_STATS=0`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` or `CI`. `AISKILLS_STATS_FOREGROUND=1 aiskills install` shows what happens.

### How do I change how these docs look?

In the single-page HTML version of these docs (`index.html`), click the gear at the top right and pick one of 11 themes; the moon/sun button next to it switches light and dark. Your choice is remembered in your browser. The default is Lights Out.

### Is there a JavaScript API?

No. Only the commands are public; the files under `src/scripts/core/` can change in any release.

### What is a skill group?

Groups come from the plugin entries in the repo's `marketplace.json`; every bundled skill is in one. See [Skill groups](concepts/skill-groups.md).

### Why isn't `newsletter-ai` in the package?

The repo's `skills/newsletters/.skillsignore` leaves it out on purpose, so `aiskills` doesn't install it. It is still in the repo, so you can install it straight from there:

```bash
npx skills add sugatoray/aiskills --skill newsletter-ai --global
```

or through `aix`, naming the source (pinned, so it isn't asked about): `aix install -s sugatoray/aiskills@newsletter-ai`.

### Nothing was installed by `npm install -g`

- **Symptom:** `aiskills installed` shows nothing after the npm install.
- **Cause:** that's expected. `npm install` only adds the `aiskills` command; the package has no install step, so it never changes your agents by itself.
- **Fix:** run `aiskills install`. It prints each step, and any error.

### `skills: not found` when run through `npx @sugatoray-ai/aiskills`

- **Cause:** an npm setting reached the nested `npx`. `aiskills` removes npm's own variables before running `npx`, so this means a new one got through.
- **Fix:** install the package with `npm install -g` and run `aiskills install`, and please [report it](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/issues).

### A pattern does nothing, or matches files

- **Cause:** the shell expanded an unquoted pattern, such as `-s scrolls-*`, into file names.
- **Fix:** quote it: `-s 'scrolls-*'`.

### A skill's `.gitignore` is missing in the package

- **Cause:** npm drops files named `.gitignore`. The package stores them as `_gitignore`.
- **Fix:** none needed: every sync renames them back in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/`.

### `--route` can't find a skill I know exists

- **Cause:** the name isn't an exact match, several skills share it, or there's no network access to `skills.sh`.
- **Fix:** run `aiskills find <name>` and pass the exact `owner/repo@skill`. See [Errors](reference/errors.md#external-skills---route).

### `... is not an aiskills folder ...`

- **Cause:** `AISKILLS_HOME` points at a folder with other files in it, which `aiskills` refuses to replace or delete.
- **Fix:** point it at a new or empty folder. See [Errors](reference/errors.md#not-an-aiskills-folder).

### `aiskills` is gone, but the skills are still installed

- **Cause:** npm ran no step on `npm uninstall -g`.
- **Fix:** `npx @sugatoray-ai/aiskills uninstall --purge`. See [Remove everything](guides/remove-everything.md).

See also: [Errors and exit codes](reference/errors.md) · [Docs home](README.md)

# License

The `@sugatoray-ai/aiskills` npm package is licensed under Apache-2.0. Each skill it bundles keeps its own license, declared in that skill's `SKILL.md`; today every bundled skill is MIT, not Apache-2.0.

## The package

| Part | License | Declared in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The npm package: the `aiskills`, `ais` and `aix` commands and their code | [Apache-2.0](../../LICENSE) | `package.json` (`"license"`), `LICENSE` |

The skills come from the [sugatoray/aiskills](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills) repo, whose own `LICENSE` covers them too.

## What this means

- **Running `aiskills`** (installing, listing, removing skills) uses the package, under Apache-2.0.
- **Using, copying or changing a skill** follows that skill's license in the table above.
- **External skills** you add with [`--route`](reference/cli.md#--route) or `aix` aren't part of the package; each keeps the license its own source gives it.

This page is generated from `package.json` and the skills' own `SKILL.md` files by `npm run docs:skills`.

See also: [Bundled skills](skills/README.md) · [Security model](concepts/security.md)
